title: Grateful Dead Live at West Palm Beach Auditorium on 1982-09-11
lineage: Master Soundboard Cassette > Reel to Reel > DAT> CDR

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1982 show with a smoking Let It Grow and an iconic Scarlet > Fire, captured on a solid soundboard that’s generally clear but has occasional mix imbalances.
ai_review.review: The performance is consistently praised as a “smoker,” highlighted by blistering versions of Let It Grow, Scarlet > Fire, Sailor > Saint and a tight Truckin’/Stella Blue pair.  The soundboard source delivers crisp overall clarity, though several listeners note that Jerry’s guitar can sit low in the mix while Brent’s keyboards dominate at times.  Despite those minor balance quirks, the show’s energy is described as high‑octane and the recording remains highly listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and rave about the musical performance; a few note mix issues but they do not detract from overall enjoyment, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear for an early‑’80s cassette soundboard; occasional level spikes and mix imbalances (Jerry low, Brent heavy) are mentioned but not severe.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as solid and tight, second set builds into a standout Scarlet > Fire segue that drives the momentum; overall pacing is praised as “just right.”

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is frequently called “out of his head,” with soaring solos on Let It Grow and Scarlet > Fire, though a few reviewers note his level sits low in the mix during parts of the second set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh provides a tight, fast groove that underpins the Scarlet > Fire transition; his bass playing is described as “smooth and tight.”
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals are highlighted as strong throughout, especially on Sailor > Saint and the later songs; his rhythm work is solid.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland receives praise for fiery solos (TLEO, Let It Grow) and a heavy presence in the mix; keyboards are called “awesome” and a key driver of the second‑set energy.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann deliver tight, layered drumming with notable pre‑drum builds; their interplay is described as “smooth and fast,” adding power to the Terrapin and Truckin' sections.
